findings.title: The SendGrid client used for cancellations is never authenticated
findings.body: This route calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the new cancellation logic uses the separate `@sendgrid/client` instance at line 57. Unlike `@sendgrid/mail`, that client is never given `SENDGRID_API_KEY` via `client.setApiKey`. Consequently the POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be rejected as unauthorized, the catch block only logs the failure, and cancelled email reminders remain scheduled and are sent.

findings.title: The one-hour cancellation window can miss reminders cancelled shortly before delivery
findings.body: The cron only attempts a SendGrid cancellation for reminders whose scheduled date is within one hour, but it runs every 15 minutes. For example, after a run at 10:00 has processed the next hour, a booking cancelled at 10:01 with a reminder due at 10:05 is not processed until 10:15, after SendGrid has already delivered it. The implementation needs to cancel at cancellation time or maintain a safety margin greater than the cron interval so a cancelled booking cannot send a reminder before the next cron pass.

findings.title: Rescheduling still creates unbounded pending SendGrid cancellations
findings.body: The reschedule path passes `immediateDelete: true`, which POSTs a SendGrid `status: cancel` request and then returns without marking or deleting the local `WorkflowReminder`. The old booking remains in the database, so the cron never sees `cancelled: true` and cannot manage this record. Each reschedule therefore leaves a cancelled SendGrid scheduled-send entry until its delivery date, recreating the pending-cancellation accumulation and 100-cancellation-limit failure this PR is intended to fix; it also leaves stale workflow-reminder rows locally.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation state updates are fired without awaiting them
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but this loop does not collect or await their promises. The request can proceed to completion (and, in a serverless runtime, be torn down) before the email reminder's `cancelled` flag is persisted. If that update is lost or delayed, the cron will not cancel the SendGrid send and the cancelled booking can still receive a reminder. Await these operations, e.g. with `Promise.all`, before returning.
